code_safety.reason: the source this server declares holds no code — only documentation, configuration or data files — so there was nothing to scan (the ruleset covers python, javascript, typescript and go)

evidence.label: authentication_model
evidence.detail: credential requirement present; enforcement partially evidenced

evidence.label: transport_security
evidence.detail: declared endpoint(s) are HTTPS: https://project-context.fairmind.ai/mcp/mcp; scored 80, not 100: `03` §4 reserves 100 for HTTPS *with HSTS*, and an HSTS header can only be seen by connecting, which `04` §9 does not do. This is an unverifiable band, not an observed absence.

evidence.label: secret_handling
evidence.detail: no committed credential found, and no environment variable with a credential-shaped name is read anywhere in the source

evidence.label: authorization_granularity
evidence.detail: no tool registration was recognised anywhere in the source. An MCP server registers tools by definition, so this is a gap in our detection rather than a server with none, and `03` §4's threshold cannot be applied to it.

evidence.label: issue_responsiveness
evidence.detail: lifetime median (2 issue(s) in the last 6 months, under `03` §5's floor of 3): 40.7 day(s) to first maintainer comment

evidence.label: release_cadence
evidence.detail: this repository publishes neither releases nor version tags

evidence.label: bus_factor
evidence.detail: no author reached `03` §5's 5-commit bar in the last 12 months (1 contributor(s) with fewer) — scored at §5's weakest described band, which the section defines for a quiet sole maintainer

evidence.label: repository_signals
evidence.detail: `03` §5 scores this by quartile WITHIN the server's category, which needs a distribution across every scanned server and so cannot be computed while scanning one. It is a post-pass over the crawl and that pass does not exist yet.

dependency_health.reason: the source this server declares holds no code and no dependency manifest, so there is no dependency to check

evidence.label: license
evidence.detail: LICENSE present with no SPDX-License-Identifier tag; identified as 'MIT' from its text

evidence.label: readme_quality
evidence.detail: README.md: exposed tools or resources enumerated (+30), states what the server does in the first 200 words (+20)

evidence.label: declared_scopes
evidence.detail: neither the README nor the MCP manifest documents what the server accesses or what side effects it has

evidence.label: changelog
evidence.detail: no CHANGELOG in the fetched source. `03` §7's partial credit for tagged releases carrying release notes is not applied here — that needs the forge API, which this check does not call

evidence.label: security_contact
evidence.detail: no SECURITY.md and no disclosure contact in the README, so a finder has no route to report a vulnerability privately
